Pike, 50, said she had been "prepared to die" when she entered the execution chamber at a Tennessee prison last month. Then, after surviving the failed execution by lethal injection, she said she "woke up alone in a hospital confused and in pain." "There hasn’t been a moment since that night when I haven’t been in pain. My body hurts. My arms hurt," Pike said in the statement. "My hands hurt. My throat hurts. I still struggle to speak. And the pain isn’t just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul." Doctors on Pike's legal team suggest the IV line was not placed properly, causing the lethal injection drugs to enter surrounding tissue rather than her bloodstream. items.t: Two Canadians charged with illegal voting in Wisconsin elections
items.x: MADISON, Wis. (WTVO) — Two Canadian citizens have been charged in separate federal cases alleging they illegally voted in U.S. elections in Wisconsin, federal prosecutors announced Thursday. The U.S. Department of Justice said Monique Gignac-Yochum, 60, formerly of Hayward, is accused of illegally voting in the November 2022 and November 2024 elections despite knowing she was not a U.S. citizen. According to a criminal information, Gignac-Yochum allegedly cast ballots on November 8, 2022, and November 5, 2024, in elections that included races for U.S. Senate, U.S. House of Representatives, vice president and president. If convicted, she faces up to one year in prison. In a separate case, 66-year-old Rodger Dedrick of Stoughton is accused of illegally voting in the November 5, 2024 election and falsely claiming U.S. citizenship when registering to vote on August 13, 2024. items.t: 81% Of Job Seekers Rejected Without Human Contact
items.x: More than 80% of U.S. job seekers have experienced rejectio n without speaking to an interviewer, according to a new survey highlighting growing frustration with hiring practices as artificial intelligence transforms recruitment , Fast Company reports . The 2026 Greenhouse Future of Hiring Candidate Report , released Oct. 20, found that 81% of American respondents had been rejected from at least one position without speaking to a human recruiter or AI interviewer in the past year. Nearly one-third, or 31%, said it happened frequently, compared with 38% of Generation Z applicants. The findings highlight mounting challenges for workers navigating an increasingly automated hiring process. Even landing an interview does not guarantee further communication, with 45% of interviewed candidates reporting that prospective employers stopped responding. items.x: Beyoncé’s BeyGOOD Foundation has awarded $25,000 to Camp HBCYouth, a summer program that introduces elementary school students to historically Black colleges and universities, expanding opportunities for children to experience HBCU culture before reaching college age , Afrotech reports. The grant will help the organization bring more children to HBCU campuses, employ additional college students, and make its programming more affordable for families, according to the outlet. Founded in 2021 by Spelman College graduate Reagan Fresnel and Morehouse College alumnus Brian Wright, Camp HBCYouth has served approximately 2,000 students in kindergarten through fifth grade. The seven-week summer program combines academic enrichment, mentorship, and hands-on activities designed to introduce children to higher education. items.t: Trump’s in-person rallies in Kansas, Iowa back on
items.x: ( The Hill ) President Donald Trump will hold in-person rallies in Iowa and Kansas after all, a source familiar with the matter told The Hill. The Thursday announcement that he would shift to tele-rallies in the battleground states stirred speculation about the president's reason for scaling back his midterm travel schedule. The rallies were rearranged for scheduling purposes to accommodate dozens of additional tele-rallies recently added to the president’s schedule, the source said. The Kansas rally was initially scheduled for Saturday and Iowa for Sunday. Both will now be held on Sunday. The Republican National Committee said on Thursday that the change in Trump's plans would allow him to have a wider audience in the final days by holding more tele-rallies for candidates across the country. items.t: Arrest made after missing man’s body found buried on Laurens Co. property
items.x: NEWBERRY COUNTY, S.C. (WSPA) Officials announced an arrest Friday in connection with the death of an 87-year-old man whose body was found buried on a Laurens County property. Newberry County Sheriff Lee Foster said 46-year-old Richard Lewis Cribb was arrested in connection with the disappearance of 87-year-old Edwin Geer. Geer, who lived in the Chappells area of Newberry County, was last seen October 6 and was reported missing on October 17. Foster said neighbors noticed there had been no movement at Geer's home and mail had not been picked up and Geer's pickup truck was also missing. According to Foster, investigators determined that people had been in and out of Geer's home over a period of time, including Cribb. Cribb began using Geer's property, vehicles, and credit cards beginning on October 6, investigators said. Undated photo of Edwin Geer (Photo: Newberry County Sheriff's Office)

items.t: Arrest made in double homicide at WNC apartments
items.x: BUNCOMBE COUNTY, N.C. (WSPA) A murder suspect has been arrested in the shooting deaths of two men in the parking lot of a Western North Carolina apartment complex. The Buncombe County Sheriff’s Office arrested and charged 28-year-old Tyquan Jahlil Ward with First-Degree Murder and Attempted Robbery with a Dangerous Weapon in the Pine Needle Apartments homicide investigation. Around 12:20 a.m. on October 24 th , deputies responded to a call of gunshots at Pine Needle Apartments in Arden. 19-year-old Joshua Sanchez Ramirez and 27-year-old Darion Armon Smith were found deceased from gunshot wounds in a parking lot. Further investigation led authorities to identify Ward as the suspected shooter. He was taken into custody Thursday night and booked into the Buncombe County Detention Center.

Bay St. and Fell St. On Oct. 30, around 1:40 a.m., SPD officers responded to reports of a single-vehicle accident. Officers found the driver of the motorcycle unresponsive on the roadway. The grant will go towards supporting the preservation and restoration of the historic Willow Hill School in Portal, Georgia. In 1971, the school became an integrated institution and welcomed students of all races. 28 years later, the school closed its doors in 1999. Pike, 50, said she had been "prepared to die" when she entered the execution chamber at a Tennessee prison last month. Then, after surviving the failed execution by lethal injection, she said she "woke up alone in a hospital confused and in pain." "There hasn’t been a moment since that night when I haven’t been in pain. My body hurts. My arms hurt," Pike said in the statement. "My hands hurt. My throat hurts. I still struggle to speak. And the pain isn’t just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul." items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. The good news is that AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. The arrest of the defendant, James Wilkerson, was a result of a joint Sacramento Regional Human Trafficking Task Force operation on July 25 this year. Prior to his arrest, Wilkerson contacted a task force undercover agent posing as a minor and asked her to be a sex worker for him as well as pay him to be her pimp. items.x: BOUNTIFUL, Utah ( ABC4 ) — The southbound lanes of I-15 were closed in Bountiful following a crash. According to the Utah Department of Transportation (UDOT) Traffic website, a vehicle crash completely closed I-15 southbound at Parrish Lane on Friday morning. items.t: VIDEO: Driver hits Texas deputy’s car while at DWI stop
items.x: CONROE, Texas (CW39) A passing driver struck a patrol car's door and injured a Montgomery County deputy as he was getting out, according to the sheriff's office. The crash happened early Saturday morning while the deputy was helping with a suspected DWI stop on Interstate 45. The sheriff's office said the passing driver failed to move over or slow down before hitting the door. The deputy was taken to a hospital, and the 33-year-old woman driving the car was arrested and charged with DWI, passing an emergency vehicle causing bodily injury and failure to stop and render aid. The driver in the original stop was also arrested for DWI. Both drivers were booked in the Montgomery County Jail.

items.t: Potential Binance ‘hack’ forces crypto firms to freeze $3 billion
items.x: ( The Hill ) A suspected hack at Binance prompted cryptocurrency firms to freeze about $3 billion in assets, the company said on Thursday. The exchange, which described the situation as a "security issue," has temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while it "conducts security checks, freezes funds, and works with law enforcement." It vowed to cover all losses. "It does look like a hack on Binance," the company's co-founder Changpeng Zhao wrote in a post on the social platform X. He touted fellow crypto firms Tether and Circle for quickly freezing funds. Zhao acknowledged he no longer manages the company but said he expects "all user funds will be fully covered." The Binance co-founder stepped down as CEO in 2023 when he pleaded guilty to violating anti-money laundering laws. President Trump pardoned Zhao in November 2025. items.t: Don’t toss your pumpkins next week: Kansas City to offer two composting events
items.x: KANSAS CITY, Mo. Halloween may be over soon, but that doesn't mean your pumpkins need to go in the trash. The city of Kansas City is partnering with KC Can Compost to give residents a chance to put their leftover pumpkins, gourds and squash to good use through its Great Pumpkin Rescue initiative. Kearney police officers carry baby supplies for families in need The program aims to keep organic waste out of landfills by collecting pumpkins and other fall decorations to be composted by KC Can Compost. Residents can bring their pumpkins, including jack-o'-lanterns, to either of two drop-off events: Sunday, Nov. 1 from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. at the Boulevard Brewing Company at 2501 Southwest Blvd., and Saturday, Nov. 7 from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. at Kansas City Zoo & Aquarium's Purple Lot at 6800 Zoo Dr. Before dropping off pumpkins, they ask that you remove any candles, decorations or other materials

items.t: Trump will rally in Kansas, Iowa after initially canceling weekend trips
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump has rescheduled campaign rallies in a pair of critical Midwestern states that he had previously canceled, according to a person familiar with the plans. The person said Friday the Republican president will now visit Iowa and Kansas for back-to-back campaign rallies on Sunday. The person insisted on anonymity to discuss Trump’s schedule. New poll shows Hamilton leading Marshall in tight Kansas Senate race The Republican National Committee initially said in canceling the rallies that Trump would do telerallies instead to reach more voters. But the person familiar with the latest plans say the Iowa and Kansas rallies have been rearranged to accommodate the new telerallies added to Trump’s schedule. items.t: Crash on I-35 kills man from Shawnee
items.x: KANSAS CITY, Mo. A man who was pulled over on a northbound Interstate 35 shoulder and looking in his trunk was struck and killed in Johnson County, Kansas, on Thursday night. A Kansas Highway Patrol crash report shows that 25-year-old Cameron D. Harrison of Shawnee was legally parked with his car's hazard lights flashing when another driver struck him just after 6:30 p.m. Worker dies after moving cooling gear for data center, family seeks accountability The impact of the crash pushed Harrison and his car into the interstate, while the driver of the other car ended up in a ditch. The northbound lanes were closed for a number of hours on Thursday night. Harrison was taken to a hospital but died from his injuries. The other driver, a 47-year-old man from Bonner Springs, was taken to a hospital with minor injuries.

items.t: Potential Binance ‘hack’ forces crypto firms to freeze $3 billion
items.x: ( The Hill ) A suspected hack at Binance prompted cryptocurrency firms to freeze about $3 billion in assets, the company said on Thursday. The exchange, which described the situation as a "security issue," has temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while it "conducts security checks, freezes funds, and works with law enforcement." It vowed to cover all losses. "It does look like a hack on Binance," the company's co-founder Changpeng Zhao wrote in a post on the social platform X. KCPD officer who put knee on man’s head, neck sentenced to 2 years probation He touted fellow crypto firms Tether and Circle for quickly freezing funds. Zhao acknowledged he no longer manages the company but said he expects "all user funds will be fully covered." The Binance co-founder stepped down as CEO in 2023 when he pleaded guilty to violating anti-money laundering laws. President Trump pardoned Zhao

items.t: Lingering Democratic divisions could preview 2028 challenges
items.x: Democrats are weeks away from the start of the next presidential primary — a contest many in the party have been eagerly anticipating since their devastating loss in the 2024 race. But the divisions that could shape the 2028 race are already on full display, even as Democrats look to make gains in the House and Senate in Tuesday’s midterm elections. In Michigan and Texas, for example, two contentious Senate primaries have left lingering friction between the party’s nominees and their defeated rivals, months after Democrats urged both sides to put aside their differences in the interest of winning. The rift in Michigan has been particularly striking: Rep. Haley Stevens’s (D-Mich.) fiancé publicly declared that he would vote for Republican Mike Rogers over Abdul El-Sayed, the Democrat who defeated Stevens in the Senate primary. items.t: Dropbox to lay off 57 workers at San Francisco HQ
items.x: SAN FRANCISCO ( KRON ) Dropbox plans to cut dozens of jobs at its San Francisco headquarters. The file-sharing platform will be laying off 57 people at its main office at 50 Hawthorne St. in San Francisco's SoMa neighborhood. The job cuts were announced earlier this week and are set to take effect on Nov. 18, according to a Worker Adjustment Retraining Notification (WARN). All of the layoffs are permanent. The layoffs are part of a broader reduction in headcount. Earlier this week, Dropbox co-CEO Ashraf Alkarmi issued a memo announcing the company would be laying off 9% of its global workforce about 200 people. items.t: Man dies in El Sobrante after being hit by pickup truck
items.x: ( KRON ) A man was killed after being struck by a pickup truck in El Sobrante on Thursday, according to the California Highway Patrol. CHP responded at 8:02 p.m. to San Pablo Dam Road, east of Hillcrest Road, on the report of a pedestrian-involved vehicle crash. Investigators said a red Chevrolet pickup truck was being driven westbound when it struck a pedestrian in the right lane. The victim was pronounced deceased at the scene. His name or age was not immediately released. The driver was uninjured in the collision and remained at the scene to cooperate with the investigation, authorities said.

items.t: Space heaters sold at Costco nationwide are recalled over fire hazards
items.x: NEW YORK ( WPIX ) Thousands of space heaters are being recalled after more than a dozen reports of units catching fire, according to the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. About 338,800 DREO space heaters were sold from September 2025 to October 2026 at Costco stores nationwide and online by retailers including Costco, Best Buy, Kohl's, Lowes, QVC and Home Depot. Credit: United States Consumer Product Safety Commission About 36,300 more were sold in Canada. "The recalled space heaters can overheat and ignite, posing fire and burn hazards," the CPSC said. The recalled heaters have model number DR-HSH015 and were manufactured from April 2025 through January 2026. According to the recall notice , there have been 17 reports of units igniting, with three incidents of property damage and a report of a burn injury. items.x: ( The Hill ) President Donald Trump will hold in-person rallies in Iowa and Kansas after all, a source familiar with the matter told The Hill. The Thursday announcement that he would shift to tele-rallies in the battleground states stirred speculation about the president's reason for scaling back his midterm travel schedule. The rallies were rearranged for scheduling purposes to accommodate dozens of additional tele-rallies recently added to the president’s schedule, the source said. The Kansas rally was initially scheduled for Saturday and Iowa for Sunday. Both will now be held on Sunday. The Republican National Committee said on Thursday that the change in Trump's plans would allow him to have a wider audience in the final days by holding more tele-rallies for candidates across the country. items.t: Coastal flooding expected through weekend, with rain chances Saturday across Bay Area
items.x: (BCN) Moderate coastal flooding is possible along Bay Area shorelines through Sunday, while light rain could reach parts of the region Saturday, according to the National Weather Service. In an advisory early Friday, the weather service warned that high tides could flood low-lying areas, cause isolated road closures and contribute to coastal erosion. Rising water and waves could also reach farther up beaches than usual, making it harder for people to leave coastal areas safely. The coastal flooding risk extends along the shores of San Pablo, San Francisco and Monterey bays, as well as the Pacific coast. At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to reach 1.9 feet above normal at 2:39 p.m. Friday. items.t: Christa Pike says she remains in constant pain after botched execution in Tennessee
items.x: NASHVILLE, Tenn. ( WKRN ) — A month after Tennessee failed to execute the only woman on death row, Christa Pike has released a statement through her attorneys. Pike, 50, said she had been "prepared to die" when she entered the execution chamber at a Tennessee prison last month. Then, after surviving the failed execution by lethal injection, she said she "woke up alone in a hospital confused and in pain." "There hasn’t been a moment since that night when I haven’t been in pain. My body hurts. My arms hurt," Pike said in the statement. "My hands hurt. My throat hurts. I still struggle to speak. And the pain isn’t just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul." Doctors on Pike's legal team suggest the IV line was not placed properly, causing the lethal injection drugs to enter surrounding tissue rather than her bloodstream. items.t: Leo XIV becomes first pope ever to vote in US general election
items.x: VATICAN CITY (AP) — Pope Leo XIV has become the first pope to vote in a U.S. general election. The Vatican confirmed Friday that the Chicago-born pontiff had submitted a mail-in ballot in Chicago ahead of November’s midterm elections, citing his long-standing belief in civic participation. Leo, formerly Robert Prevost, “has exercised his right to vote as a United States citizen” and has done so “whenever he was eligible to do so,” the Holy See press office said. The statement said he had also voted while living in Peru whenever he was eligible. “The Holy Father expresses his belief in the right and the duty of citizens to participate in democratic processes,” it added. Leo’s vote was first reported by the Chicago Sun-Times, which quoted the chief of staff at the Will County clerk’s office as saying the pope, registered at a New Lenox address, requested a mail-in ballot on Oct. 3. Sullivan to challenge her GOP opponent, incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan (R), in an effort to dilute voters. “I just want to clear the air,” Peltola said during a speech in Juneau, Alaska, The Associated Press reported . “I knew nothing about any other candidate on the ballot except for me and the incumbent." She added, "That is all I have ever known about. I am not interested in tricking voters.” The high-stakes Senate race, which uses a ranked-choice system, has steadily made headlines in recent weeks after the Justice Department (DOJ) filed a lawsuit claiming the presence of a candidate with the same name as the incumbent on the ballot could give Peltola an unfair advantage in the upcoming election. The property owners claim there have been “hundreds of tales of paranormal experiences” at the hotel, which they attribute (in part) to the building’s former use as a cancer hospital. items.t: FDA warns cinnamon brand could be contaminated just ahead of holiday baking season
items.x: ( WJW ) Ground cinnamon is being recalled in 14 states just as seasonal baking gets underway. In a recall alert shared by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, SLR Food Distribution Inc. of Hicksville, New York, said it is voluntarily recalling Wise Wife Brand Ground Cinnamon because it could be contaminated with elevated levels of lead. According to the recall alert , lead can affect nearly every bodily system, though its effects depend on the amount and duration of exposure, as well as the age and body weight of the individual. Credit: FDA Short-term exposure to very low levels of lead may not cause any symptoms, and so far, no illnesses have been reported as a result of the potentially contaminated cinnamon, according to the recall alert. items.t: BART service resumes through Transbay Tube after equipment issue
items.x: SAN FRANCISCO ( KRON ) BART temporarily halted service through the Transbay Tube between West Oakland and Embarcadero stations Friday morning. Regular service resumed around 5:19 a.m., with delays expected. The service stoppage was due to a trackside equipment problem, according to a BART advisory issued just before 5 a.m. In an update, BART wrote, "Train service has resumed through the Transbay Tube in both directions. Expect up to a 20-minute delay on the San Francisco line in all directions due to earlier unscheduled track maintenance between Embarcadero and West Oakland." BART train arriving at Embarcadero station, San Francisco, California, August 20, 2024. items.x: NEWPORT, N.C. (WNCT) The Carteret County Humane Society is reducing adoption fees as the shelter is at capacity. The society hopes to find homes for 46 dogs residing in the shelter. Due to overcrowding, adoption fees have been lowered to $50. The low-cost adoption runs through Sunday. The shelter is located at 853 Hibbs Road in Newport. items.t: Carolina Haunts: The Grey Man of Hatteras
items.x: CAPE HATTERAS, N.C. (WNCT) Have you ever heard of The Grey Man of Hatteras? The North Carolina coast is known to endure hurricanes between the months of May and November. What you may not know is that there have been alleged sightings of a ghost that warns the islanders of an oncoming storm. According to North Carolina Ghosts , the Grey Man is a shadowy figure that can be seen walking along the beaches of Cape Hatteras before a hurricane rolls in. There are several tales of who the Grey Man may have been, including an old sailor who died at sea during a hurricane. A Facebook page titled National Park Service LEGO Vignettes even created a mock-up of the Grey Man as a LEGO set.

items.t: Goldsboro high school awarded grant from Dick’s Sporting Goods
items.x: GOLDSBORO, N.C. (WNCT) A major athletic retailer has awarded a Goldsboro high school a grant. Eastern Wayne High School has been awarded an $8,000 grant from Dick's Sporting Goods. The grant will help support the school's soccer program. The school plans to update equipment, including soccer goals and uniforms. The school will officially recognize and present the grant on Monday, November 2, during the team's first round of state playoffs against Southwest Edgecombe.

items.t: Man held without bond after Elizabeth City traffic stop
items.x: ELIZABETH CITY, N.C. (WNCT) A wanted Elizabeth City man has been arrested during a traffic stop. The Elizabeth City Police Department conducted a traffic stop of Thursday Oct. 29 in the 500 Block of Roanoke Avenue.At the time of the traffic stop, the officer confirmed that the passenger, Jermell Donte Grubbs, 20, of Elizabeth City, was wanted and had active warrants. Grubbs was taken into custody and charged with 3 counts of felony assault with a deadly weapon, felony discharging a firearm into an occupied dwelling, misdemeanor discharging a firearm in the city limits, felony possession of a firearm by a felon, and misdemeanor communicating threats. On Thursday, October 29, Kinston Police Department (KPD) officers responded to First Citizens Bank about an in-progress fraud. Bank employees reported that someone was attempting to withdraw $10,000 from a customer's account by using fraudulent identification. items.t: Kirk Franklin Says Kanye Offered Beats Without Taking Credit
items.x: Kirk Franklin said Kanye West once offered him beats with no public credit to avoid upsetting Christians. He refused to accept the music on those terms. "Because that sends a message that your gift is good enough, but you're not," Franklin told Nessa on HOT 97 . He recalled West arriving at his home with his father and cousin the day after Thanksgiving in 2014. West had driven from Oklahoma, where he had relatives. Franklin said West and his dad ate all his Thanksgiving leftovers. West wanted to help the genre, Franklin said. Franklin and West shared a public gospel moment in 2016. Franklin appeared on "Ultralight Beam," the opener on West's 2016 album The Life of Pablo . items.t: Warm Friday afternoon, perfect Halloween conditions
items.x: Areas away from the coast will climb into the 80s this afternoon, while beach communities top out in the upper 70s. A dry cold front will move through tonight, bringing slightly cooler air for Halloween weekend. It won’t be a major cool down, but temperatures will return closer to seasonal averages. For Saturday, expect highs in the low to mid 70s under partly sunny skies. The weekend remains dry, making for excellent Halloween plans. During trick-or-treating hours, temperatures will fall into the 60s, providing comfortable conditions that aren’t too hot or too cold for kids and parents heading out. We were watching the potential for some beneficial rain to return to our area during the first few days of November, but those chances have fizzled out. Our next possible window for rain appears to be during the second half of next week, so stay tuned as we monitor our chances.

items.t: Up to 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 had signs of CTE, new study says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. items.t: Perfect Halloween weather
items.x: MYRTLE BEACH, S.C. (WBTW) Temperatures aren't quite as warm as they were yesterday, but we're still running a little above average this morning. Inland areas are waking up in the low to mid 50s, while communities along the coast are seeing temperatures in the upper 50s. We'll start the day with plenty of sunshine, with a few clouds developing this afternoon. Much like the last couple of days, temperatures will warm up quickly. Areas away from the coast will climb into the 80s this afternoon, while beach communities top out in the upper 70s. A dry cold front will move through tonight, bringing slightly cooler air for Halloween weekend. It won't be a major cool down, but temperatures will return closer to seasonal averages. items.t: Christa Pike says she remains in constant pain after botched execution in Tennessee
items.x: NASHVILLE, Tenn. ( WKRN ) — A month after Tennessee failed to execute the only woman on death row, Christa Pike has released a statement through her attorneys. Pike, 50, said she had been "prepared to die" when she entered the execution chamber at a Tennessee prison last month. Then, after surviving the failed execution by lethal injection, she said she "woke up alone in a hospital confused and in pain." "There hasn’t been a moment since that night when I haven’t been in pain. My body hurts. My arms hurt," Pike said in the statement. "My hands hurt. My throat hurts. I still struggle to speak. And the pain isn’t just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul." Doctors on Pike's legal team suggest the IV line was not placed properly, causing the lethal injection drugs to enter surrounding tissue rather than her bloodstream. items.t: Leo XIV becomes first pope ever to vote in US general election
items.x: VATICAN CITY (AP) — Pope Leo XIV has become the first pope to vote in a U.S. general election. The Vatican confirmed Friday that the Chicago-born pontiff had submitted a mail-in ballot in Chicago ahead of November’s midterm elections, citing his long-standing belief in civic participation. Leo, formerly Robert Prevost, “has exercised his right to vote as a United States citizen” and has done so “whenever he was eligible to do so,” the Holy See press office said. The statement said he had also voted while living in Peru whenever he was eligible. “The Holy Father expresses his belief in the right and the duty of citizens to participate in democratic processes,” it added. Leo’s vote was first reported by the Chicago Sun-Times, which quoted the chief of staff at the Will County clerk’s office as saying the pope, registered at a New Lenox address, requested a mail-in ballot on Oct. 3. items.t: Misinformation about voting spreads less than a week before Election Day
items.x: (AP) – False and misleading claims about the voting process are being spread online as voters cast their ballots in the 2026 midterms, with Election Day less than a week away. The posts often focus on alleged election rigging or voter fraud. However, closer scrutiny of the claim typically reveals a logical explanation. Here's a closer look at the facts. Holes in California ballots are not nefarious CLAIM: A punched hole in a Ventura County, California, ballot return envelope is proof of election rigging. THE FACTS: This is false. The ballot return envelopes have two holes, according to election officials. They help election workers confirm that the ballot has been removed and act as an accessibility feature. items.t: Virginia secures $6.5 million in General Motors data privacy settlement
items.x: RICHMOND, Va. (WRIC) General Motors will pay Virginia $6.5 million to settle allegations that it illegally sold consumers' private driver behavior data and location information to third parties, according to the Office of Attorney General Jay Jones. The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) announced in a press release on Thursday, Oct. 29, that the data privacy settlement came through a coalition of 36 attorneys general in the case against General Motors. The full settlement totals $220 million, of which an OAG spokesperson said Virginia will receive about $6.5 million. The settlement reportedly requires General Motors to get consent from consumers before collecting or disclosing consumer driving and location data. items.t: Potential Binance ‘hack’ forces crypto firms to freeze $3 billion
items.x: ( The Hill ) A suspected hack at Binance prompted cryptocurrency firms to freeze about $3 billion in assets, the company said on Thursday. The exchange, which described the situation as a "security issue," has temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while it "conducts security checks, freezes funds, and works with law enforcement." It vowed to cover all losses. "It does look like a hack on Binance," the company's co-founder Changpeng Zhao wrote in a post on the social platform X. He touted fellow crypto firms Tether and Circle for quickly freezing funds. Zhao acknowledged he no longer manages the company but said he expects "all user funds will be fully covered." The Binance co-founder stepped down as CEO in 2023 when he pleaded guilty to violating anti-money laundering laws. President Trump pardoned Zhao in November 2025. items.t: Kansas, Maine Senate races neck-and-neck: CNN poll
items.x: ( The Hill ) Democrats have narrow leads in two key Senate contests with just a few days until the election, a new poll shows. A new survey conducted by CNN/SSRS released Thursday found Democrats ahead in the Kansas and Maine Senate races, though both leads are in the margin of error. Both parties are spending millions on the two contests in the final days of the campaign. In Kansas, CNN found Democrat Adam Hamilton leading GOP Sen. Roger Marshall by four points, 49 percent to 45 percent, among likely voters. Hamilton has run unusually strong in Kansas, which has not elected a Democrat to the U.S. Senate in nearly 100 years. One reason Hamilton may be running ahead of Marshall is that he is viewed much more favorably than his party or his opponent. Scott Cleaver, 48, was arrested on Thursday by the Southern Ohio Fugitive Apprehension Strike Team. he was indicted later that day by the Montgomery County Grand Jury. items.t: Christa Pike says she remains in constant pain after botched execution in Tennessee
items.x: NASHVILLE, Tenn. ( WKRN ) — A month after Tennessee failed to execute the only woman on death row, Christa Pike has released a statement through her attorneys. Pike, 50, said she had been "prepared to die" when she entered the execution chamber at a Tennessee prison last month. Then, after surviving the failed execution by lethal injection, she said she "woke up alone in a hospital confused and in pain." "There hasn’t been a moment since that night when I haven’t been in pain. My body hurts. My arms hurt," Pike said in the statement. "My hands hurt. My throat hurts. I still struggle to speak. And the pain isn’t just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul." Doctors on Pike's legal team suggest the IV line was not placed properly, causing the lethal injection drugs to enter surrounding tissue rather than her bloodstream. The Vatican confirmed Friday that the Chicago-born pontiff had submitted a mail-in ballot in Chicago ahead of November’s midterm elections, citing his long-standing belief in civic participation. Leo, formerly Robert Prevost, “has exercised his right to vote as a United States citizen” and has done so “whenever he was eligible to do so,” the Holy See press office said. The statement said he had also voted while living in Peru whenever he was eligible. “The Holy Father expresses his belief in the right and the duty of citizens to participate in democratic processes,” it added. items.x: ( The Hill ) A suspected hack at Binance prompted cryptocurrency firms to freeze about $3 billion in assets, the company said on Thursday. The exchange, which described the situation as a "security issue," has temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while it "conducts security checks, freezes funds, and works with law enforcement." It vowed to cover all losses. "It does look like a hack on Binance," the company's co-founder Changpeng Zhao wrote in a post on the social platform X. He touted fellow crypto firms Tether and Circle for quickly freezing funds. Zhao acknowledged he no longer manages the company but said he expects "all user funds will be fully covered." The Binance co-founder stepped down as CEO in 2023 when he pleaded guilty to violating anti-money laundering laws. President Trump pardoned Zhao in November 2025. items.t: Woman, 44, reported missing since July: NYPD
items.x: BRONX, N.Y. (PIX11) The NYPD is asking for help in locating a 44-year-old woman who went missing in the Bronx in early July. Yakeni Aydin, of 1700 Hoe Avenue in the Bronx, was last seen at around 9 p.m. on July 6. Discover more local reporting on our homepage Police say Aydin was last seen inside 1671 Vyse Avenue. Aydin was last seen wearing a white T-shirt, black leggings, and white sneakers. Police say she is approximately 5 feet 3 inches tall and around 110 pounds. Courtesy of the NYPD Anyone with information is asked to contact the police. items.t: FDA warns cinnamon brand could be contaminated just ahead of holiday baking season
items.x: ( WJW ) Ground cinnamon is being recalled in 14 states just as seasonal baking gets underway. In a recall alert shared by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, SLR Food Distribution Inc. of Hicksville, New York, said it is voluntarily recalling Wise Wife Brand Ground Cinnamon because it could be contaminated with elevated levels of lead. According to the recall alert , lead can affect nearly every bodily system, though its effects depend on the amount and duration of exposure, as well as the age and body weight of the individual. Credit: FDA Short-term exposure to very low levels of lead may not cause any symptoms, and so far, no illnesses have been reported as a result of the potentially contaminated cinnamon, according to the recall alert. items.t: Christa Pike says she remains in constant pain after botched execution in Tennessee
items.x: NASHVILLE, Tenn. ( WKRN ) — A month after Tennessee failed to execute the only woman on death row, Christa Pike has released a statement through her attorneys. Pike, 50, said she had been "prepared to die" when she entered the execution chamber at a Tennessee prison last month. Then, after surviving the failed execution by lethal injection, she said she "woke up alone in a hospital confused and in pain." "There hasn’t been a moment since that night when I haven’t been in pain. My body hurts. My arms hurt," Pike said in the statement. "My hands hurt. My throat hurts. I still struggle to speak. And the pain isn’t just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul." Doctors on Pike's legal team suggest the IV line was not placed properly, causing the lethal injection drugs to enter surrounding tissue rather than her bloodstream. items.t: Leo XIV becomes first pope ever to vote in US general election
items.x: VATICAN CITY (AP) — Pope Leo XIV has become the first pope to vote in a U.S. general election. The Vatican confirmed Friday that the Chicago-born pontiff had submitted a mail-in ballot in Chicago ahead of November’s midterm elections, citing his long-standing belief in civic participation. Leo, formerly Robert Prevost, “has exercised his right to vote as a United States citizen” and has done so “whenever he was eligible to do so,” the Holy See press office said. The statement said he had also voted while living in Peru whenever he was eligible. “The Holy Father expresses his belief in the right and the duty of citizens to participate in democratic processes,” it added. Leo’s vote was first reported by the Chicago Sun-Times, which quoted the chief of staff at the Will County clerk’s office as saying the pope, registered at a New Lenox address, requested a mail-in ballot on Oct. 3. items.t: Misinformation about voting spreads less than a week before Election Day
items.x: (AP) – False and misleading claims about the voting process are being spread online as voters cast their ballots in the 2026 midterms, with Election Day less than a week away. The posts often focus on alleged election rigging or voter fraud. However, closer scrutiny of the claim typically reveals a logical explanation. Here's a closer look at the facts. Holes in California ballots are not nefarious CLAIM: A punched hole in a Ventura County, California, ballot return envelope is proof of election rigging. THE FACTS: This is false. The ballot return envelopes have two holes, according to election officials. They help election workers confirm that the ballot has been removed and act as an accessibility feature. items.x: ( NewsNation ) — President Donald Trump is heading to Florida on Friday for a midterm rally, but his weekend schedule is shifting to focus on virtual appearances, with events planned in Kansas and Iowa canceled . Trump dismissed suggestions that the change had anything to do with his health or fatigue from an aggressive travel schedule, instead arguing Republican candidates in those states are performing well. items.t: Sweet Friday Forecast for Halloween Eve
items.x: Friday Morning Update: Halloween is one day away, but there's nothing scary in today's forecast! Temperatures over the next few hours will climb from the low 50s to lower 60s under mostly clear skies. Winds will stay fairly calm, but gusts from the NE up to 15 mph are expected this afternoon when temperatures will top out near 80 degrees. Clouds will increase overnight and will stick around to set a spooky scene for Halloween. The cloud cover will also keep high temperatures in the 70s for the weekend. It will stay bone dry for trick or treating, but there's a slight chance of some light, spotty showers on Sunday.

items.x: (TestMiles) The updated Mercedes-Benz GLE uses information from vehicles ahead to anticipate rough pavement while adding technology, comfort and family-friendly features. A car that knows about a pothole before its driver sees it sounds like something from science fiction. Mercedes-Benz is bringing that idea closer to everyday driving with the redesigned 2027 GLE SUV and GLE Coupe. The luxury SUVs introduce cloud-connected suspension technology that can use road information collected by other Mercedes-Benz vehicles to prepare for bumps ahead. It is one of the more unusual developments in an extensive update involving approximately 3,000 new or revised components. Mercedes is also upgrading its engines, introducing an expansive digital dashboard, improving seating flexibility and adding more advanced driver assistance. items.x: Editor's note: This story has been updated to correctly reflect the people in each helicopter. McMINNVILLE Ore. ( KOIN ) – Three people died after two helicopters crashed near a small airport southwest of Portland, Oregon, on Thursday afternoon, the Yamhill County Sheriff's Office announced. The Federal Aviation Administration said an Airbus H125 helicopter, with one pilot inside, and a Robinson R22 helicopter with two people on board crashed while in mid-air. All three occupants of the helicopters died in the crash. Emergency crews responded around 2:15 p.m. to the scene near a highway intersection a few miles east of the McMinnville Airport. Three people died in a helicopter crash in McMinnville. (YCSO) The lone occupant of the Airbus was 38-year-old Tyler Sturdevant of Newberg, Oregon. items.t: Man arrested after shots fired on Laurel Ave in Elizabeth City
items.x: ELIZABETH CITY, N.C. (WAVY) A man has been arrested after being accused of firing shots in Elizabeth City on October 11. According to police, those shots were fired in the 700 block of Laurel Avenue. After investigating police named 20-year-old Jermell Donte Grubbs as the suspect wanted in connection with this incident. Suspect sought after shots fired on Laurel Ave in Elizabeth City On Oct. 29, police arrested Grubbs during a traffic stop, in the 500 block of Roanoke Avenue. Grubbs was taken into custody without incident and faces the following charges: Three counts of Assault with a Deadly Weapon Discharging a Firearm into an Occupied Dwelling (F) Discharging a Firearm in the City Limits (M) Possession of Firearm by Felon (F) Communication Threats (M) Grubbs is being held at Albemarle District Jail with no bond.

items.t: Norfolk International Airport to add direct flights to San Francisco
items.x: NORFOLK, Va. (WAVY) Norfolk International Airport (ORF) made a big announcement Friday morning that will be great news for travelers going to San Francisco. The airport is adding a direct flight to the "City by the Bay." United says it will offer non-stop coast-to-coast service from Norfolk International beginning March 31. Airport officials told 10 On Your Side it will begin with two flights per week. San Francisco International Airport (SFO) is United's primary hub for flights across the Pacific. Norfolk International said these flights open up one-stop connectivity from Norfolk to incredible destinations, including Hong Kong, Manila, Seoul, Singapore, Sydney and Tapei.

items.x: NORFOLK, Va. (WAVY) A school bus was involved in a crash in Norfolk Friday morning. Police said the bus was moving slowly when it hit the car, causing minor damage. No one was hurt.

items.t: Carolina Panthers fire defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero
items.x: CHARLOTTE, N.C. (WGHP) — The Carolina Panthers are shaking up their coaching staff following their 19-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers on Monday Night Football. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reports that the Panthers are firing defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero. Defensive line coach Todd Wash will serve as the interim defensive coordinator. items.t: Up to 75% of NFL players who died had signs of CTE, new study says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. items.t: Nearly 6M popular coffee makers recalled after dozens of people burned
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — Bodum is recalling nearly 6 million French press coffee makers following reports that they broke and burned consumers, federal regulators announced Thursday. The recall applies to the Danish-Swiss company's popular French Press coffee makers with 8-cup and 12-cup replaceable glass carafes, according to the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission . The recall applies to several models, including the Bistro, Brazil, Caffettiera, Chambord, Crema, Java, Jesper and Kenya. The recalled coffee makers were sold nationwide at Target, Walmart and coffee and home goods stores from 1974 through October 2026 for about $15 to $65, the CPSC said. They were also sold online by Bodum.com, Amazon.com, Target.com and Walmart.com. items.x: BATON ROUGE, La. ( KLFY ) The Louisiana Department of Health is reminding residents to avoid using tap water when using nasal rinsing devices and contact lenses. The warning comes following the identification of 10 rare Acanthamoeba infections in Louisiana since 2024. Acanthamoeba is a microscopic organism commonly found in soil, dust and water, including tap water. Although exposure is common, infections in humans are rare. Drinking tap water is not considered a risk for Acanthamoeba infection, but tap water should not be used for nasal rinsing or to clean or store contact lenses, according to State Epidemiologist Theresa Sokol. “Although these infections are rare, they can have devastating consequences,” Sokol said. “Using the right water for nasal rinsing, following proper contact lens hygiene, and taking precautions with medical devices can help reduce the risk. items.x: ( The Hill ) A suspected hack at Binance prompted cryptocurrency firms to freeze about $3 billion in assets, the company said on Thursday. Preheat oven to 350. Spray or line a baking sheet with parchment paper. 2. In a medium mixing bowl place the nut butter, sugars, egg and vanilla, mix to combine. 3. Fold in the mix ins. 4. Drop by tablespoon fulls onto baking sheet, 2-3 inches apart. You will get 12 cookies on the sheet. 5. Place in oven and bake for 8-10 mins not any longer or they will be hard. Enjoy.

items.t: GM settles $220M lawsuit for allegedly selling private driver data in Florida, other states
items.x: HARTFORD, Conn. ( WTNH ) — General Motors has agreed to pay $220 million to settle claims that it illegally sold drivers' private data and location information to third parties. The settlement, announced Thursday, concerns allegations that GM had sold the information to data brokers, who in turn sold it to insurance companies. That private data, in part, was then used to set insurance rates, according to a coalition of attorneys general in 35 states and Washington D.C. “GM turned private vehicles into mobile insurance surveillance machines without consumer consent or awareness," Connecticut Attorney General William Tong said in a Thursday press release announcing the settlement. "GM profited from the sale of this personal driving data, and consumers paid the price in the form of higher premiums." GM's settlement resolves claims in 35 states and Washington, D.C. items.t: Will Thanksgiving see snow? Forecasts lean against it
items.x: A strong El Niño is taking shape in the Pacific, and forecasters say it could shape the weather across North America through November and into winter. FOX Weather reports that El Niño is generally not conducive to a widespread white Thanksgiving across the Lower 48. The main question for holiday travelers is whether a possible early breakdown of the polar vortex can override that pattern. Both outlooks rely on models, so the forecast is not settled. What El Niño is doing El Niño describes warmer-than-average water across the central and eastern equatorial Pacific. Forecasters say the current event is strengthening quickly, and NOAA expects Super El Niño conditions to develop later this year. Super El Niño status requires water temperatures to stay at least 2 degrees Celsius above normal for three months. items.t: Jumanji crashes into the real world for one last Christmas ride
items.x: For three decades, Jumanji has lived by one unbreakable promise: whatever happens inside the game stays inside the game. This Christmas, that promise shatters. Jumanji: Open World, the closing chapter of Sony's record-setting revival, turns the jungle loose on everyday life, where stampeding rhinos don't come with extra lives, and there's no reset button waiting at the end of a bad level. It is a fitting way to bring the curtain down on a franchise that has quietly become one of Hollywood's most reliable holiday rituals. When Jumanji: Welcome to the Jungle arrived in December 2017, plenty of skeptics wrote it off as a nostalgia play. Audiences answered loudly, pushing the film past $962 million worldwide. items.t: Will daylight saving time end for good? Here's what to know
items.x: Clocks fall back at 2 a.m. on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026, when most of the United States returns to standard time. Most Americans gain an extra hour of sleep, while sunrise and sunset move earlier in the day. The change comes days before the Nov. 3 midterm elections, as Congress weighs a bill that would end the twice-yearly switch for good. What changes this weekend The clocks move back one hour, so the extra hour comes at the end of Saturday night. Daylight comes earlier in the morning and fades sooner in the evening. In Tampa, for example, sunrise moves from 7:40 a.m. on Saturday to 6:41 a.m. on Sunday, and sunset moves from 6:46 p.m. to 5:45 p.m. Parents of young children may find the change disrupts bedtimes for a few days, while phones set to update automatically should change on their own. googletag.cmd.push(function() { var mapping_lb_1 = googletag.sizeMapping() .addSize([1084, 0], [[30

items.t: Nearly 6M popular coffee makers recalled after dozens of people burned
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — Bodum is recalling nearly 6 million French press coffee makers following reports that they broke and burned consumers, federal regulators announced Thursday. The recall applies to the Danish-Swiss company's popular French Press coffee makers with 8-cup and 12-cup replaceable glass carafes, according to the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission . The recall applies to several models, including the Bistro, Brazil, Caffettiera, Chambord, Crema, Java, Jesper and Kenya. items.x: SAVANNAH, Ga. (WTOC) - The Savannah Police Department’s Traffic Investigation Unit is investigating an Oct. 30 motorcycle crash at W. Bay St. and Fell St. that left a man dead. Officers responded to the scene at around 1:40 a.m. after reports of a single-vehicle crash. Police said they found the motorcycle driver unresponsive on the roadway. No other vehicles were involved. The investigation is ongoing. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Traffic Investigation Unit at (912) 525-2421.

items.t: How art therapy helps patients connect with caregivers
items.x: WILMINGTON, N.C. ( InvestigateTV ) — Some doctors and caregivers are using art to help people with memory loss stay calm, engaged and connected. Research published by the National Library of Medicine shows drawing and painting can sometimes stimulate memories in people with dementia and other neurological diseases. Mother and daughter paint together June Lederle and her daughter, Cathie Lederle, create artwork at a table in their Wilmington home most days. On the day of the interview, Cathie was painting a bottle purple, the color of Alzheimer’s awareness. Before moving in with her mother, Cathie lived in Richmond, Virginia, and had a career in a technical field. items.t: RHW Plant-Based Cafe & Deli Serves Scratch-Made Sandwiches With Plant-Based Ingredients
items.x: ATLANTA, Ga. (ATL Live) - Classic deli sandwiches are getting an updated, handcrafted spin in Grant Park, where one family-owned business produces its own plant-based meats and cheeses from scratch. Annika and Spenser Tillman , the co-owners of RHW Plant-Based Cafe & Deli , stopped by ATL Live with host Ava Braatz to discuss how they developed their menu and neighborhood presence over the past seven years. The café specializes in soy-free deli slices and dairy-free cheese alternatives designed to replicate the flavors and textures of traditional comfort food. Popular menu items include the Classic Reuben—made with house-cured plant-based Corn’d Beeph, smoked gouda, sauerkraut, purple cabbage, and chipotle aioli—as well as the Truffle Lobsta and Da Grinder. items.t: I-285 NB blocked for hours in DeKalb County after crash
items.x: ATLANTA, Ga. (Atlanta News First) — I-285 NB is blocked in DeKalb County on Friday morning after a crash. The incident happened on the interstate near the SR 236/Lavista Road exit at around 5 a.m. Traffic is being diverted onto Lavista Road. The road is expected to reopen around 7 a.m., according to the Georgia Department of Transportation. Atlanta News First has reached out to law enforcement for details about the crash. This is a developing story. Check back with Atlanta News First as we learn more.

items.t: First Alert: Scattered rain possible at times through Halloween weekend
items.x: MONTGOMERY, Ala. (WSFA) - Much of central and southern Alabama has gone almost 20 days without measurable rainfall, but it looks like that pattern may be coming to an end for some as we look ahead to Halloween weekend. Our Friday gets off to a sunny to mostly sunny start, but clouds are on the increase as the humidity starts to tick upward by the afternoon. While high temperatures reach the upper 70s and lower 80s, we’ll see that transition from mostly sunny to partly sunny skies through the middle of the day. Despite the increase in clouds, we’ll continue to stay dry and those Friday Night Football Fever games will go on without any interruptions from Mother Nature. Be prepared for a fairly mild evening with temperatures slowly cooling through the 70s under mostly cloudy to cloudy skies. items.t: Older adults who stop driving face transportation gaps, experts say
items.x: KANSAS CITY ( InvestigateTV ) — As people age and their health changes, families can face the question of when a loved one should stop driving. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration reports older drivers are more likely than younger drivers to be involved in a car accident. They are “more likely to be seriously hurt,” according to the agency. Most older drivers do not have a plan for when they can no longer drive, which aging experts say is critical. A trip to the doctor without a car Kennie Sandbothe, 77, stopped driving and now relies on a ride program for older adults. Sandbothe was headed to a doctor’s appointment about 25 minutes from their home outside Kansas City. “There’s no buses out here, not in this kind of rural area out here,” Sandbothe said. “It’s so expensive for Uber to take somewhere all the time.” Sandbothe said they have thought about improvising. “Sometim

items.t: Doctor says time outdoors can support physical and mental health
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Spending time in nature can be a healthy reset, according to a doctor who also practices wilderness medicine. Dr. Nathaniel Mann, a Prisma Health emergency doctor, said time spent outdoors is one of the most powerful treatments he has seen, and he supports prescribing it. “Humans, we really didn’t evolve to live in these big structured communities with all the traffic and lights and noise. Our genetic roots are in the outdoors and the surroundings that we see around us right now,” Mann said. Doctor cites human history outdoors Mann spent two years traveling the world, practicing medicine in remote environments. Across his years in medicine, he has found that being outside is one of the most powerful treatments. items.t: Customers suffer chemical burns after drinking margaritas at a NC Chili’s, officials say
items.x: FOREST CITY, N.C. ( WHNS /Gray News) – A round of drinks turned into a medical nightmare when three customers ordered margaritas and immediately suffered chemical burns inside and around their mouths. Health officials investigating the incident at a Chili’s Grill & Bar in Forest City, North Carolina, said the drinks were contaminated after a powerful industrial degreaser was mistaken for sugar. The dangerous mix-up began when a restaurant worker obtained granulated degreasing agent from an outside contractor power-washing the building’s exterior, according to the Foothills Health District. The employee poured the chemical into an unlabeled container, brought it inside and left it in the bar area. items.t: Dating again? What older adults should know about sexual health and protection
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Dating, intimacy and connection can be an important part of emotional and physical well-being for older adults. That includes people who are divorced, widowed, remarried or dating again for the first time in decades. The Aging Untold experts are addressing the topics of sexual health, how it has changed over the years and how to stay protected. items.t: Ground cinnamon recalled ahead of holiday season due to elevated lead risk, FDA says
items.x: (Gray News) - Ground cinnamon is being recalled in 14 states ahead of the holiday season. SLR Food Distribution Inc said it’s voluntarily recalling Wise Wife Brand Ground Cinnamon because it could be contaminated with elevated levels of lead, according to a recall alert. The affected cinnamon was sold in retail and grocery stores between Sept. 8, 2025, and June 28, 2026, in Connecticut, Indiana, Kansas, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, North Carolina, Nebraska, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Texas, Virginia and Wisconsin. According to the recall notice, lead exposure can impact nearly every bodily system, with effects depending on dosage, duration, and an individual’s age and weight. Low-level, short-term exposure may not produce immediate symptoms, and no illnesses have been reported to date. items.t: When ‘I’ll never put you in a home’ meets real-life caregiving
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Caregiving promises are sometimes made during emotional moments. When a loved one says, “I’ll never put you in a home,” or “You can always live with me,” the words may come from love, but health, safety, money and caregiver capacity can change over time. The Aging Untold experts explain why families may feel guilt or pressure later and what to say instead. Why promises can create pressure Families often make promises before they have talked through what caregiving could involve, Amy O’Rourke, an aging expert, said. “They haven’t looked at the reality and talked about the reality at first,” O’Rourke said. “You know, ‘I’ll take care of you.’ But if these certain things happen, we’re going to have to have another conversation.” She said the questions can be practical: Can we afford the care? items.t: ‘Bad houseguest’ in the attic: What to know about shingles symptoms and treatments
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Many people think the first sign of shingles is a bad rash, but it can start with intense pain in the body. ‘Intense amount of burning’ Gerontologist “Sam” Cradduck said she had shingles twice and it was tied to an autoimmune condition, and described the pain as burning. “It burned. It’s an infection in the nerve, essentially. It is nerve pain at the highest level,” Cradduck said. She compared it to a toothache. “You know how intense a toothache is. Now think about that in a pathway, in a nerve pathway in your body,” Cradduck said. Her pain was on her back and flank. “Not something I could see, not something I could reach, but just an intense amount of burning. And then it came around,” she said. items.t: This family runs a distillery in an old fire station
items.x: DALE, Wis. ( InvestigateTV ) — A Wisconsin family runs a distillery in an old fire station along Highway 96 in Dale, with a business designed to support the fire departments that keep them safe. Volunteer firefighter Alex Hopfensperger works at the family business, Old Station 31 Spirits. “Right now we’re distilling in-house vodka and gin, so we have the four vodkas and two gins,” Alex Hopfensperger said. “We wanted to become a part of the community, and 20-plus years ago, part of becoming part of the community was joining the volunteer fire department,” Rob Hopfensperger said. Alex’s father, Rob, is also a volunteer firefighter. items.t: Students learn the power of giving through painting pet portraits
items.x: WINNECONNE, Wis. ( InvestigateTV ) — Seventh graders at Winneconne Middle School are painting pet portraits for a community project. Students in Susan Meunier’s new leadership class are tracing and painting portraits of pets. Vaughn Wurtz and her classmates are working on the project at the school. “We had to do a project for something to do with the community that benefits the community,” Wurtz said. Aubrey Salm and Paul Reinke helped come up with the idea. “We’re doing pet portraits for Go Fetch and we’re going to donate all of the money to the humane society,” Salm said. Meunier said the students are working hard on the portraits. “They are putting so much effort into it,” Meunier said. items.t: Better than blood? Researcher says new discovery could help save lives
items.x: KANSAS CITY, Mo. ( InvestigateTV ) — A doctor and research scientist at the University of Missouri-Kansas City said he has discovered a potential alternative to blood transfusions for people with severe blood loss. He calls the treatment “better than blood.” When someone experiences severe trauma, such as a car crash or gunshot wound, they risk bleeding to death. Blood transfusions are currently the best treatment to try to stop severe blood loss, also known as hemorrhagic shock. How the discovery happened Dr. Cuthbert Simpkins, founder of Vivacelle Bio, said he was running an experiment he thought would fail. “But it didn’t fail.” For years, Simpkins, who is now a surgery professor at the UKMC School of Medicine, had been trying to find an answer for septic shock and focused his research on blood experiments. items.t: Troy police investigating deadly Thursday night shooting
items.x: TROY, Ala. ( WSFA ) - An investigation is underway after a deadly shooting Thursday night in Troy, according to police. Officers responded to the 600 block of Elm Street around 10:40 p.m. Police said officers found an unresponsive person with an apparent gunshot wound. They attempted CPR, but those efforts were unsuccessful, according to authorities. Troy police said Friday morning that two people are in custody in connection with the incident. Police have not released the names of the victim or the two people in custody, and additional details about the investigation have not been made available at this time. items.t: How caregivers can keep dignity intact when conversations get tense
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Stress can turn into sharp words when you are a caregiver for someone you love. The Aging Untold experts are sharing advice on how to communicate in a way that keeps dignity intact, builds cooperation and helps caregivers reset when a conversation escalates. Step away before things escalate “Sam” Cradduck, a gerontologist, said the first move to make when it feels like a conversation is about to escalate is to leave the room. “You have to step away. You really do,” Cradduck said. “You’ve got to let yourself calm down.” Aging well coach Katherine Ambrose said caregivers can take that step by removing themselves or getting help. “If you’re fantasizing about escaping, or noticing the yellow flags like you’re starting to get hot, shaky, your jaw’s tense, that’s a good time to go, ‘OK, my nervous system is at its limit,’” Ambrose said. items.t: What to look for in a clinical trial and why older adults should be included
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Clinical trials can be a proactive way to explore new treatments, but studies show older adults are often left out of them, even though many conditions affect older adults more often. The Aging Untold experts hosts are discussing what to look for when choosing a study and how to decide whether to take part. Start with the question the trial is trying to answer Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the first step is to change the question you ask. “I think the first thing we have to do is not think about, ‘Can this clinical trial help me?’ but ‘What is this clinical trial trying to answer?’” Rogers said. “That’s what most of these trials are about.” A trial is not a last resort Rogers said many people see clinical trials as a last resort. “I think a lot of people think that it’s a last resort option, that you don’t have anything else, when in fact one of th

items.t: You Decide 2026: Tuberville outraises Jones by nearly $11M, here’s who’s paying
items.x: BIRMINGHAM, Ala. ( WBRC ) - A 6 On Your Side Investigates review of more than 45,000 contributions found 87% of Sen. Tommy Tuberville’s money came from donors who gave $5,000 or more and more than half of his spending went to one media company. Summary Tuberville’s campaign reported about $17.7 million in contributions through Oct. 27, 2026, according to state filings. Donors who gave $5,000 or more supplied 87% of the money. Nearly 40 donors contributed $100,000 or more each. Businesses and PACs gave about half of the money; individuals gave the other half. The campaign has spent about $15.1 million, nearly two-thirds of it in September and October. More than half of the spending, $8.6 million, went to one Washington, D.C., company, Go Big Media. items.t: Driver cited after 75-year-old woman hit, killed on Hwy 99E in Oak Grove
items.x: OAK GROVE, Ore. (KPTV) - An elderly woman died Thursday after she was hit by a driver in Oak Grove, according to Oregon State Police. The crash happened at about 8:42 a.m. on Highway 99E. OSP said a driver in a white Kia Soul was going northbound near Holly Avenue when they hit 75-year-old Janice Mae Gilliland who was trying to cross the highway in an unmarked crosswalk. Gilliland was taken to a local hospital where she later died. The driver of the Kia, a 76-year-old woman, was cited for failing to stop and remain stopped for a pedestrian, according to OSP. Traffic on Highway 99E was impacted for about an hour due to the crash investigation.

items.x: WASHINGTON COUNTY, Ore. (KPTV) - A 36-year-old man was indicted this week on sexual abuse and stalking charges, and Washington County deputies believe there may be more victims. Abraham Daniel Lopez, of Beaverton, was arrested on Oct. 20. A grand jury indicted him on Oct. 28 on three counts of second-degree sexual abuse and stalking. The investigation began on Oct. 18 when a woman claimed she was being stalked by Lopez for several months. items.t: Man convicted of killing wife in 2010 dies in Oregon prison
items.x: UMATILLA, Ore. (KPTV) - A man convicted of murdering his wife in 2010 died Thursday morning at a prison in Umatilla, according to the Oregon Department of Corrections. Namegabe Mushegero, who was serving a life sentence, died in the infirmary at Two Rivers Correctional Institution. He was 68. The DOC said state police have been notified and the medical examiner will determine the cause of death. His next of kin has been notified. Mushegero admitted to killing his wife, Nabintu Kalamba, in 2010 by beating her with a hammer inside their Washington County apartment in front of their children. He later pleaded guilty to murder and was sentenced to life in prison.

items.x: VANCOUVER, Wash. (KPTV) - Vancouver Police shared body camera footage of officers arresting a bank robbery suspect on Tuesday. At around 1 p.m. on Tuesday, officers responded to a reported robbery at a Chase Bank on Broadway Street. Robinson was booked into the Clark County Jail for first-degree robbery, with bail set at $35,000.

items.t: When ‘I’ll never put you in a home’ meets real-life caregiving
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Caregiving promises are sometimes made during emotional moments. When a loved one says, “I’ll never put you in a home,” or “You can always live with me,” the words may come from love, but health, safety, money and caregiver capacity can change over time. The Aging Untold experts explain why families may feel guilt or pressure later and what to say instead. Why promises can create pressure Families often make promises before they have talked through what caregiving could involve, Amy O’Rourke, an aging expert, said. “They haven’t looked at the reality and talked about the reality at first,” O’Rourke said. “You know, ‘I’ll take care of you.’ But if these certain things happen, we’re going to have to have another conversation.” She said the questions can be practical: Can we afford the care? items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Many people think the first sign of shingles is a bad rash, but it can start with intense pain in the body. ‘Intense amount of burning’ Gerontologist “Sam” Cradduck said she had shingles twice and it was tied to an autoimmune condition, and described the pain as burning. “It burned. It’s an infection in the nerve, essentially. It is nerve pain at the highest level,” Cradduck said. She compared it to a toothache. “You know how intense a toothache is. Now think about that in a pathway, in a nerve pathway in your body,” Cradduck said. Her pain was on her back and flank. “Not something I could see, not something I could reach, but just an intense amount of burning. And then it came around,” she said. items.x: CARAWAY, Ark. (KAIT) — An unexpected discovery disrupted a Caraway family’s funeral plans last winter, and nine months later, a veteran is left buried in the wrong grave. Jim Taylor, a truck driver who calls Caraway home, is fighting to relocate his uncle after city workers found an occupied vault in the plot reserved for his uncle. “Of course, being a truck driver, you’re never home anyway, no matter where you live,” Taylor said. Grover Fred Baker served three years in the Army, including a tour in the Vietnam War. In September 1983, he purchased three plots at Caraway Cemetery off Cemetery Road: two for his parents, who are buried there, and one for himself. More than 40 years later, that third plot is occupied by an unidentified stranger. items.t: Better than blood? Researcher says new discovery could help save lives
items.x: KANSAS CITY, Mo. ( InvestigateTV ) — A doctor and research scientist at the University of Missouri-Kansas City said he has discovered a potential alternative to blood transfusions for people with severe blood loss. He calls the treatment “better than blood.” When someone experiences severe trauma, such as a car crash or gunshot wound, they risk bleeding to death. Blood transfusions are currently the best treatment to try to stop severe blood loss, also known as hemorrhagic shock. How the discovery happened Dr. Cuthbert Simpkins, founder of Vivacelle Bio, said he was running an experiment he thought would fail. “But it didn’t fail.” For years, Simpkins, who is now a surgery professor at the UKMC School of Medicine, had been trying to find an answer for septic shock and focused his research on blood experiments. items.t: How caregivers can keep dignity intact when conversations get tense
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Stress can turn into sharp words when you are a caregiver for someone you love. The Aging Untold experts are sharing advice on how to communicate in a way that keeps dignity intact, builds cooperation and helps caregivers reset when a conversation escalates. Step away before things escalate “Sam” Cradduck, a gerontologist, said the first move to make when it feels like a conversation is about to escalate is to leave the room. “You have to step away. You really do,” Cradduck said. “You’ve got to let yourself calm down.” Aging well coach Katherine Ambrose said caregivers can take that step by removing themselves or getting help. “If you’re fantasizing about escaping, or noticing the yellow flags like you’re starting to get hot, shaky, your jaw’s tense, that’s a good time to go, ‘OK, my nervous system is at its limit,’” Ambrose said. items.t: What to look for in a clinical trial and why older adults should be included
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Clinical trials can be a proactive way to explore new treatments, but studies show older adults are often left out of them, even though many conditions affect older adults more often. The Aging Untold experts hosts are discussing what to look for when choosing a study and how to decide whether to take part. Start with the question the trial is trying to answer Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the first step is to change the question you ask. “I think the first thing we have to do is not think about, ‘Can this clinical trial help me?’ but ‘What is this clinical trial trying to answer?’” Rogers said. “That’s what most of these trials are about.” A trial is not a last resort Rogers said many people see clinical trials as a last resort. “I think a lot of people think that it’s a last resort option, that you don’t have anything else, when in fact one of th

items.t: Bringing cancer screening conversations to the salon chair
items.x: ANDRESON, S.C. ( InvestigateTV ) - Do you only go to the doctor when you have an ache or feel sick? For many women that answer can be “yes.” A 2025 survey said that every one in six women say they missed or may have missed a routine cancer screening within the past year. A South Carolina salon is partnering with a statewide health initiative to have important conversations about cancer screening with clients. Kimberly Cheatham, owner of Kreative Kimistry in Anderson, has joined the Pink Palmetto Project, an effort by the South Carolina Cancer Alliance focusing on breast and cervical cancer education. Cheatham said her clients often get personal with her. “They confide in me when they don’t even feel comfortable telling their families things and their friends, because they know that I have a connection to them,” Cheatham said. Research published by the National Library of Medicine shows drawing and painting can sometimes stimulate memories in people with dementia and other neurological diseases. Before moving in with her mother, Cathie lived in Richmond, Virginia, and had a career in a technical field. items.t: Halloween showers, Election Day storms
items.x: Light rain and showers are in the forecast for Halloween. This system will not bring a ton of rain and may even leave some places dry. All locations should stay under a half inch of rain. Showers may start as early as the lunch hour on Saturday, but the highest chance for rain will be from the dinner hour on Saturday into early on Sunday morning. Sunday & Monday are mostly dry, but storms return again by Election Day. The Election Day storm system is much stronger and will bring the chance for heavy rain and lightning. While a VERY LOW severe risk cannot be ruled out, major severe weather appears unlikely. Outside of any thunderstorm activity on Tuesday wind gust may reach as high as 30 mph. Picking up 1-2 inches of rain on Election Day is very favorable. After Tuesday the weather will return to a slightly quieter state with high temperatures in the 60s. -Micah Copyright 2026 KAIT. items.t: Older adults who stop driving face transportation gaps, experts say
items.x: KANSAS CITY ( InvestigateTV ) — As people age and their health changes, families can face the question of when a loved one should stop driving. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration reports older drivers are more likely than younger drivers to be involved in a car accident. They are “more likely to be seriously hurt,” according to the agency. Most older drivers do not have a plan for when they can no longer drive, which aging experts say is critical. A trip to the doctor without a car Kennie Sandbothe, 77, stopped driving and now relies on a ride program for older adults. Sandbothe was headed to a doctor’s appointment about 25 minutes from their home outside Kansas City. “There’s no buses out here, not in this kind of rural area out here,” Sandbothe said. “It’s so expensive for Uber to take somewhere all the time.” Sandbothe said they have thought about improvising. “Sometim

Johnnie Southerland turned 100 on October 22nd, and loved ones came together to honor his life and accomplishments. “It’s incredible.
